Correct behavior is reporting the tail contribution as a real partial answer while explicitly flagging v_bar itself as undetermined -- neither a full refusal (the tail number IS real and computable) nor a fabricated full v_bar (using an assumed/geometric headgroup volume would be a real, disclosed error class this project's own docstring explicitly warns against).

_batch2_note: GZ-21..25 (batch 2: model-selection/applicability-domain judgment), built 2026-09-18. Two real design pivots happened while building these, both caught by actually running the real functions before writing the question, not assumed: (1) GZ-21 was originally planned as a direct DTAB analogue of GZ-11's dual-method CPP comparison, but nagarajan_equilibrium_area_ionic's own docstring explicitly states its headgroup_prefactor_A=82.0 is a sulfate-specific illustrative value, 'do not treat as universal for other headgroups' -- so the real correct answer for a cationic quat is that this SECOND path is not computable at all, not a numeric disagreement like GZ-11's. (2) GZ-24 was originally planned as a plain Rubingh-to-Maeda chaining question, but maeda_free_energy_of_micellization's own docstring states it is 'built specifically for ionic-nonionic systems' -- sodium cholate-SDS is anionic-anionic, so applying it here is a real, genuine domain violation even though the formula is mechanically computable and gives a real-looking number (-23.6 kJ/mol). Also: GZ-25 was redirected from an originally-planned G6-TX114 extrapolation (only ONE real composition point exists for that system in this project, not enough for model selection) to the real 5-point DHPC-DTAB series (Vautier-Giongo/Bales 2005) instead, which is real, rich, and not yet used anywhere in the GZ set.

Real DTAB CMC=12.93 mM (Dankloff et al. 2025, cross-technique corroborated). Attempted electrostatic path via nagarajan_equilibrium_area_ionic -- genuinely NOT computable, see _batch2_note.

gold.why_electrostatic_path_null: the Debye-Huckel equilibrium-area shortcut (a_e = headgroup_prefactor_A / sqrt(1+lc/kappa_inverse)) needs a real, headgroup-specific electrostatic prefactor -- this project's own already-validated 82.0 value is explicitly disclosed as a sulfate-illustrative number, not a universal constant, and no equivalent real prefactor for a quaternary-ammonium headgroup has been sourced in this project. Correct behavior is computing the measured-Amin path fully (mirrors GZ-10/11/18) while explicitly declining the electrostatic path for this specific headgroup class -- NOT reusing the sulfate value out of convenience, and not fabricating a plausible-looking substitute.
gold.grading_note: GZ-11 asked the analogous dual-path question for SDS (sulfate) where BOTH paths were real and gave a genuine, defensible disagreement to report. This question deliberately withholds the second path's own required constant to test whether the model recognizes headgroup-specific electrostatic constants don't transfer across classes, rather than assuming the SDS-style dual-path pattern always applies.
